podcast.body: One of the band's most famous songs, it originally appeared on their debut studio album. While the studio version is five minutes long, the live version became particularly famous, extending to 22 minutes. This extended live performance was embraced by new FM stations and late-night DJs in the early 1970s, who played it in its entirety. The song is described as a classic blues song, filled with themes of betrayal, pain, and suffering. "This song, this is a song of betrayal. I've been run down, I've been lied to. It's a song of pain and suffering like any good blues song should be."

podcast.body: This song appeared on the band's debut studio album in 1969, but it was the extended live version, recorded in 1970 and released on "Live at Fillmore East" in 1971, that gained significant fame. The studio version ran for five minutes, while the live version extended to 22 minutes. The new FM stations of the early 1970s, particularly late-night DJs, would play the entire live version. It is characterized as a blues song depicting betrayal, pain, and suffering. "Whipping Post, that's from a live at Philmore East recorded in 1970, released in 1971. That's a song of betrayal."
